1 · The 8 layers a PR crosses

Left to right. Bottom line = main finding.

LAYER 1
PR event
What changed? Which labels?
full label is auto-added to 95 of 100 PRs, so it says nothing about the change
LAYER 2
Trigger
GHA always on code; Buildkite MP on mp/full/force-ci
Override should be force-ci or a new mp-full
LAYER 3
Classify by path
Today: all or nothing (path-filter.sh)
Proposed: 8 change classes → required tiers (P8)
LAYER 4
Test tier
Which layers must run?
Cheap, fast gates first; heavy GPU only when the path needs it
LAYER 5
Workload / job
~35 MP jobs, 0–4 GPUs each
2,099 no-op SGLang jobs wait ~20 min, then exit in 5 s
LAYER 6
Acceptance
What does PASS mean?
~30 thresholds in 15+ files; TTFT check never runs (C9)
LAYER 7
Verdict + retry
Bug, flake or infra?
1 real code catch in 30 days; failures cluster on node 248
LAYER 8
Mergeable
Time-to-green, GPU per PR
Core-only PR: 518 → ~3 GPU-min per build (P8)

3 · Early-fail staircase (proposed)

A PR climbs only as high as its change class needs. Height = relative cost. required today jobs are named in the tooltip.

CPU only (every code PR) GPU: L1 unit pod required today; others only on path match Full: label or nightly

Target: L0 → CPU E2E finishes in ≤ 15 min. Times from P1 (p50 wall) and P4 (server bench ~20–25 s per run on WSL CPU). Layout-smoke cost is an estimate (P6).

4 · What L0 … Full mean

Lower = cheaper and earlier. A failing step stops the climb.

StepIn plain wordsRuns on / timeWhat it catchesExampleExists today?
L0 lintRead the code without running itCPU · < 1 minstyle, typos, wrong types, banned patterns (e.g. raw torch.device)pre-commit: ruff, mypy, codespell, SPDX headeryes
L1 unit · CPUOne function or class alone, fake inputsCPU · ≈19 min × py3.10–3.14 (GHA, advisory)logic bugs in one module: hashing, lookup, locks, configtest_hash_tokens_deterministic in tests/v1/multiprocess/test_token_hasher.pyyes · not required
L1 unit · GPU podSame unit suite + cuda-marked tests, on 1 GPU1 GPU · 25 min queue + 24 min (k3-unit-tests)GPU kernels, storage suites that need a device todaytest_store_and_lookup in tests/v1/multiprocess/test_cache_server.py (cuda)yes · required
L2 server scenariosStart the real LMCache server alone (no vLLM/SGLang); fake clients send store / lookup / retrieveCPU · ~25 s per scenariobugs between modules in the server: restart, metrics, L2 flow, HTTP API, concurrencylmcache bench server --scenario restart_reregisterpartly: bench exists, scenarios proposed
CPU E2EReal vLLM (CPU build) + LMCache + a tiny model, real requests end to endCPU 8 cores · ~3.6 minconnector wiring, store→hit→restart flow, output identicalcpu_e2e_validation (Buildkite, required) · same script in GHA cpu_device.yml (advisory)yes · required
L3 engine smokeReal engine on 1 GPU, short accuracy check, only for the engine the PR touches1 GPU · ~10 minGPU transfer corrupting KV silently, engine API changeslm_eval gsm8k twice → same answersexists, but runs for every PR
Layout smokeOne small or dummy-weight model per KV layout type (MLA, fp8, hybrid, SWA)1–2 GPU · est. few minKV shape / layout bugs without loading 160 GB modelsDSV4 dummy 4 layers + hma_bit_correctness.pyXPU only, not CUDA (CPU MLA dummy in GHA cpu_device, advisory)
Path add-onsOne extra GPU test that runs only when its code area changes1–2 GPU · 7–20 GPU-minrestart, P2P, GDS, preemption bugs (only these tests catch them)edit heartbeat.py → add restart_recoverytests exist, not path-triggered
Full / nightlyEverything, big models, multi-GPU, perf vs baseline1–4 GPU · ~535 GPU-minTP=4 fp8, perf regressions, engine × transport matrixdsv4_flash_tp TP=4, long_doc_qa TTFTyes: today every code PR runs this

Rule: a test lives in the lowest step that can still catch its bug.

7 · PR GPU-min in 30 days

Today vs the proposed rule (shadow run on 223 PRs).

Worst case: new tiers cost 2× the estimate and a perf canary runs on every code PR. Source: P8 §5.3.

Removing the baseline engine

Four workloads start a 2nd engine on a 2nd GPU just to compare (P5).

Baseline CV is 2–7%, so a stored baseline is viable. Total ≈ 43,200 GPU-min (≈ 23%). Overlaps with the rule saving.
